slides.title: Redis is single-threaded. So how does it use **16 CPU cores?**
slides.text: Short answer: it doesn't. You do 👉

slides.title: I/O threads help, but **not with commands**
bullets: 🔌|Parse requests and write replies in parallel
⚛️|Commands still run on ONE thread, so still atomic

cols.title: 🖥 Many instances
cols.text: One per core, ports 6379 to 6386. You route keys yourself.

slides.title: **16,384** hash slots
slides.text: Every key maps to a slot. Each master owns a range of slots.

slides.title: Hash tags keep keys **together**
slides.text: Only the part inside `{}` is hashed, so related keys share a slot and multi-key commands work.
slides.code:
{user:42}:cart
{user:42}:profile
→ same slot, same node ✅

MGET a b   (different slots)
→ CROSSSLOT error ❌

slides.title: Sharding is **not free**
bullets: 🔗|Multi-key ops and Lua need the same slot
🔥|A hot key still lives on one node

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: One Redis instance executes commands on **one core**. We use many cores by **sharding with Redis Cluster** (16,384 slots). I/O threads speed up networking, but **commands stay single-threaded**.
